messages.body_plain:

I have  small question:

diffAnn=annotateWithGeneParts(as(myDiff25p,"GRanges"),gene.obj)

> getTargetAnnotationStats(diffAnn,percentage=TRUE,precedence=FALSE)
  promoter       exon     intron intergenic
      6.43      25.70      33.33      42.57

plotTargetAnnotation(diffAnn,percentage=TRUE,precedence=FALSE)

Although the parameters are the same (x=diffAnn, precedence=FALSE), the barplots show different percentages, namely:
promoter: 6%
exon: 22%
intron: 29%
intergenic: 43%

What can I do about that?

Thank you very much!

messages.subject_clean: [methylkit_discussion] unique() for GRanges list of islands and shores
messages.body_plain:
you have to merge GRanges objects that contain shores and CpGi and feed it into the regionCounts

something like reduce(c(cpg.obj$CpGi,cpg.obj$shores)) could work.
reduce merges coordinates that overlap. Sometimes the shores of one CpG island will cover the next one, if they are close by. check reduce() function in GenomicRanges

Best,
Altuna

messages.subject: Re: [EXTERNAL] methylKit and Missing Data
messages.body_plain:
Hi Louis,

So it was a formatting issue, basically the NA’s in your input files caused the problem.
If for a certain base you do not have any signal it should be a 0 instead of NA,
which is also the format that supported software like Bismark would return for missing observations.

So you have to quick fixes that you can choose from:
 a) manually remove all rows in your input files that contain NA
or
 b) replace all NA with Zeros

Both will bring your input files in a format supported by methlyKit.

Best,
Alex

messages.subject: How to interpret histogram of CpG coverage?
messages.subject_clean: How to interpret histogram of CpG coverage?
messages.body_plain:
Hello,
I'm working with targeted bisulfite sequencing data for the first time, and therefore I am not sure how to interpret the CpG coverage histograms.

messages.subject: annotation in methylkit
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I'm trying to annotate my differentially methylated bases in methylkit. I saw that it was suggested that annotation bed files be obtained from UCSC's table browser. However, my alignment files were made using Ensembl, so there is a mismatch error when I try to annotate because of the different conventions in chromosome name between UCSC and Ensembl. Are there files I can get from Ensembl that I can manipulate to be correctly formatted for this purpose? I'm a little stuck on this. Also, I am dealing with the pig genome which was updated last year.

Thanks,
Marissa

messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] annotation in methylkit
messages.body_plain:
UCSC has Sscrofa11.1 it seems to be the same as ensembl version, you should be able to download bed files from UCSC and rename the chromosomes as ensembl convention. If you can't do that somehow, you can try to download GTF/GFF from ensembl and convert that into BED, you can search the forum on how to do that. I don't know what is the best way to make that conversion.

Best,
Altuna

messages.subject_clean: methRead reduces the dimensions of .txt files
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

RRBS data was made available to me as .txt files for each sample (n=121).
Here is the head of one sample:

chrBase chr base strand coverage freqC freqT
chr1.10470 chr1 10470 R 10 80 20
chr1.10472 chr1 10472 R 10 80 20
chr1.10485 chr1 10485 R 11 72.72 27.2727
chr1.10490 chr1 10490 R 11 72.72 27.2727
chr1.10494 chr1 10494 R 10 10 90
chr1.10497 chr1 10497 F 42 50 50
chr1.10498 chr1 10498 R 5 100 0

These files are of dimension nrow=1,403,528 ncol=7. When read using methRead they shrink in size to become nrow=777,707 ncol=7 with the exception of one sample nrow=939,852.
Has anyone encountered this before and does anyone have recommendation on how to avoid loosing this large number of sites?

Please note that these files do not contain missing data

Many thanks
